title: NVIDIA driver installer could not continue
shortDescription: GeForce driver installation aborts with a generic failure.
fullDescription: The NVIDIA installer can fail when a previous driver is partially installed, when antivirus blocks DLL registration, or when the Windows GPU is not supported by the target driver branch.

fixSteps.title: Run DDU in Safe Mode
fixSteps.instruction: Boot Windows Safe Mode and run Display Driver Uninstaller.

fixSteps.title: Clean install
fixSteps.instruction: Run NVIDIA installer and select Custom > Perform a clean install.

whenToCallPro: If hardware fault suspected, contact NVIDIA or board partner.

faq.a: Yes, widely used to cleanly remove GPU drivers.

title: GPU hung while processing a command
shortDescription: DirectX detected that the GPU stopped responding.
fullDescription: This error indicates the GPU failed to respond within the TDR window. Common causes are unstable overclocks, driver bugs, or failing hardware.

fixSteps.title: Reset clocks
fixSteps.instruction: Reset MSI Afterburner or similar to stock clocks.

whenToCallPro: If errors persist at stock settings.

faq.a: Yes, unstable system RAM can trigger hangs.

title: Display driver stopped responding and has recovered
shortDescription: Windows TDR recovered the GPU driver after a hang.
fullDescription: TDR (Timeout Detection and Recovery) kicks in when the GPU does not respond within 2 seconds. Caused by driver bugs, overclocks, or heat.

fixSteps.title: Check temperatures
fixSteps.instruction: Monitor GPU temp; clean dust if above 85C.

whenToCallPro: If the card is physically damaged.

faq.a: Not recommended; can mask hardware issues.

title: CUDA initialization or execution failed
shortDescription: Compute workloads fail on NVIDIA GPU.
fullDescription: CUDA errors in AI/rendering apps often stem from driver/CUDA version mismatch or out-of-memory conditions.

fixSteps.title: Match CUDA version
fixSteps.instruction: Install CUDA Toolkit that matches your driver.

faq.q: Do I need CUDA for gaming?

title: Windows has stopped this device because it has reported problems
shortDescription: Device Manager reports Code 43 for the GPU.
fullDescription: Code 43 indicates Windows disabled the GPU due to a reported failure. Common with driver corruption, hardware failure, or PCIe contact issues.

fixSteps.title: Clean driver reinstall
fixSteps.instruction: Use DDU and reinstall latest driver.

fixSteps.title: Reseat GPU
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove card, reseat in PCIe slot.

whenToCallPro: If persists after reinstall and reseat.

title: BSOD referencing nvlddmkm.sys
shortDescription: Blue Screen from NVIDIA display driver.
fullDescription: This BSOD occurs when the GPU driver fails to recover from a hang. Can be overclock, overheat, or PSU related.
whenToCallPro: If PSU and OC not the cause.

faq.a: Usually, but system RAM can contribute.

title: GPU thermal limit reached
shortDescription: GPU throttles or shuts down due to heat.
fullDescription: When GPU reaches ~83C (core) or ~100C (memory junction), it throttles. Dust, dried thermal paste, or poor airflow cause this.

fixSteps.title: Clean dust
fixSteps.instruction: Use compressed air on heatsink and fans.

whenToCallPro: If teardown is outside your comfort.

title: Display goes black after installing NVIDIA driver
shortDescription: Monitor shows no signal after driver load.
fullDescription: Caused by EDID conflicts, HDMI/DP mode issue, or corrupt driver install.

fixSteps.title: Boot Safe Mode
fixSteps.instruction: Hold Shift+Restart, boot Safe Mode with Networking.

fixSteps.title: DDU + reinstall
fixSteps.instruction: Clean driver and reinstall stable branch.

faq.q: Should I try DP and HDMI?

title: Control Panel not in Windows menu
shortDescription: NVIDIA Control Panel disappeared from context menu.
fullDescription: Often missing after driver updates if the Microsoft Store app is not installed.

fixSteps.title: Install from Store
fixSteps.instruction: Search 'NVIDIA Control Panel' in Microsoft Store.

title: Shader compilation errors in games
shortDescription: Games stutter or crash at shader compile.
fullDescription: Shader cache at %LOCALAPPDATA% can be corrupted after crashes.

title: GeForce Experience won't open
fullDescription: Error 0x0003 caused by disabled NVIDIA services or network adapter issues.

faq.a: Yes, use NVIDIA App or plain driver.

title: Pixel artifacts on screen
fullDescription: Lines, squares, or color corruption indicate failing VRAM or memory overclock too aggressive.

title: RTX 40-series 12VHPWR melting risk
shortDescription: Power connector not fully seated on RTX 4090.
fullDescription: Improperly seated 12VHPWR connector causes melt damage. Ensure full insertion and avoid tight bends.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Fully insert 12VHPWR until click, inspect for damage.

whenToCallPro: If connector damaged, contact NVIDIA for RMA.

title: GPU fans stopped at idle or under load
fullDescription: Many modern GeForce cards have zero-RPM mode below 50C. If fans don't start under load, check fan header or bearing.

fixSteps.title: Test fan curve
fixSteps.instruction: Use MSI Afterburner to force 50% fans and verify.

whenToCallPro: If fan bearing failed and under warranty.

faq.a: No, it's designed behavior below threshold.
